newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf Oil Outlook - Slow trade hits premium.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf Oil Outlook - Slow trade hits premium.

text.p: Business in the Gulf oil product market slowed further in the week to Thursday, with more pressure seen on middle distillate premiums, Gulf traders said.
"There is not much business at all in the Gulf at the moment," one trader said.
"It is extremely quiet. There is some tendering going on but there are very few private deals being done," said another.
They said jet was under severe pressure, trading at a premium of around five cents.
"Jet is the weakest. It is trading at around five cents plus," said one Gulf-based trader.
Another trader put the premium in a 10 to 20 cent range, but added "this very much depends on timing".
This compares to a 20 to 25 cent range last week.
Traders said that traditionally jet business was not good from about May to July.
"But this year we might see this softness continue into the third and fourth quarters," one said.
Jet was independently assessed at around $22.60 a barrel fob Gulf from $23 a week earlier.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp tender to buy jet fuel for July 1-30 delivery closes on Thursday.

Gas oil premiums were seen slightly better than those on jet, but little changed from last week. Traders said ADNOC's tender for 75,000 tonnes of 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil was awarded at a 35 cent premium.
"It was probably a little on the high side," said one trader, adding that the premium on 0.5 percent sulphur was now at 35 to 45 cents and that on one percent sulphur was between 20 and 30 cents.
Gas oil was independently assessed at $23.45 a barrel fob Gulf from around $23.25 last week.
